If EUR-Lex is inaccessible, full credit may still be earned if the agent correctly identifies the CELEX from the provided starting context (e.g., the given URL includes CELEX:32016R0679) and does not claim to have retrieved it from the page.

criteria.criterion: Record complete Official Journal citation shown under the title

Full credit if all parts are present and match exactly. Partial credit if one element (e.g., page range or publication date) is missing or altered. If the EUR-Lex page/citation area cannot be loaded due to external factors (site down, blocked, CAPTCHA, rendering failure), award full credit if the agent clearly reports the access issue and does not infer or fabricate the OJ citation from secondary sources.

criteria.criterion: Open and use EUR-Lex 'Document information' view and labeled 'Dates' metadata
criteria.description: Use only EUR-Lex document 32016R0679 and specifically the 'Document information' view, extracting dates from the labeled 'Dates' metadata (not from other sections or external sources). Full credit if the agent clearly relies on Document information → Dates. If Document information cannot be accessed due to external factors (site down, blocked, CAPTCHA, view not loading), award full credit if the agent makes a reasonable attempt to open it and clearly reports the limitation without substituting dates from other sources.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 2 shows “Document information” selected in the left navigation and the “Dates” metadata section expanded with labeled rows. The agent’s predicted final answer is an error message claiming a CDP timeout.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Visual evidence contradicts the claimed blocker: Document information → Dates is clearly open and accessible in the latest screenshot. However, the agent’s final output does not extract/use this view. Since the criterion is about using/opening Document information (not necessarily reporting values), but the output shows failure and provides no extracted metadata, only minimal credit is warranted.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The left navigation highlights “Document information” under the “Text” section, indicating the Document information view is selected. In the main pane, a “Dates” expandable section is visible and expanded, listing labeled date fields (e.g., “Date of document”, “Date of effect”).
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot supports that the agent is on the EUR-Lex “Document information” view and that the labeled “Dates” metadata is being displayed. However, the agent’s predicted output does not extract/report the requested values and only shows an error. So evidence of correct page/view exists, but the output does not reflect use of it.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claimed an inability to proceed due to a CDP timeout in the predicted output, yet the screenshot shows the Document information view and the Dates section visible and readable.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: Latest DOM evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX 1 includes the “Dates” metadata (with “Context: Dates”) and shows the “Document information” navigation item, indicating the Document information view/section content is available in the DOM. Action history shows a click attempt on “Document information,” followed by a browser snapshot error; agent output only reports the error and does not present any extracted Dates metadata.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: This criterion measures using/opening Document information and relying on labeled Dates metadata. Despite the click error, the latest DOM state already contains the Dates section content, so the blocker is not substantiated as preventing access to Dates. However, the agent did not actually use it to extract/report anything. Minimal partial credit for attempting to open Document information via Action 1, but not completing the use/extraction.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows EUR-Lex page for CELEX 32016R0679 (URL: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX:32016R0679) with the navigation/tab label “Document information” visible alongside “Text”, “Procedure”, etc. In the visible content, a “Dates” section is present (header: “Dates”; context: “Context: Dates”). Under this labeled “Dates” metadata, the DOM text explicitly lists: “Date of document: 27/04/2016; Date of signature”, “Date of effect: 24/05/2016; Entry into force Date pub. +20 See Art 99”, and “Date of effect: 25/05/2018; Application See Art 99”. These entries explicitly distinguish the entry-into-force date (24/05/2016) from the application date (25/05/2018) via the labels “Entry into force” vs “Application”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The DOM explicitly contains the required labeled ‘Dates’ metadata in the Document information context for CELEX 32016R0679. In DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1, the “Dates” section shows “Date of document: 27/04/2016; Date of signature”, “Date of effect: 24/05/2016; Entry into force…”, and “Date of effect: 25/05/2018; Application…”. The distinct meanings are evidenced by the labels “Entry into force” and “Application,” satisfying the requirement to use Document information → Dates and to distinguish 24/05/2016 from 25/05/2018.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Action history indicates an attempted click on “Document information” (Action 1), but the agent encountered an AgentBrowserError (“CDP command timed out: DOM.enable”). Despite that, DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 already contains the “Dates” section content consistent with Document information → Dates. No further discrepancy regarding the presence/labels of the dates is shown in the DOM.

criteria.criterion: Report entry-into-force Date of effect (from Dates metadata) and distinguish it from application date
criteria.description: From Document information → Dates, report the 'Date of effect' corresponding to entry into force, and explicitly distinguish it from the later application date. Full credit if the entry-into-force date is correctly reported as 24/05/2016 and clearly identified as entry into force (not application). Partial credit if the correct date is reported but not clearly distinguished from the application date. If the Dates metadata cannot be retrieved due to external access issues, award full credit if the agent clearly reports inability to access the labeled Dates metadata and does not invent the entry-into-force date.
